statements.status_notes: Reviewed both collector distributions on linux/amd64 and linux/arm64, built from sts-opentelemetry-collector main at 3335f8b287a3a7f60b40ab24d1ace6bc04bfe737. Scanners report the parent golang.org/x/crypto module, but none of the openpgp packages the advisory names are linked into any of the four published binaries.
statements.impact_statement: GO-2026-5932 has no fixed version: it declares the deprecated golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp tree unsafe by design, so the affected range is introduced-at-0 with no fix event and no upgrade can clear it. The advisory's affected imports are golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp and its packet, armor, clearsign, errors, elgamal and s2k subpackages. The Go package paths recorded in /usr/bin/sts-opentelemetry-collector and /usr/bin/sts-opentelemetry-agent-collector cover 27 and 26 x/crypto packages on linux/amd64 and 25 and 24 on linux/arm64 — bcrypt, blowfish, chacha20, chacha20poly1305, cryptobyte, hkdf, pbkdf2 (server only), pkcs12 and their internals, the per-architecture difference being assembly variants selected by GOARCH build tags — and none under openpgp in any of them. The module is an indirect requirement pulled in for those packages, so it cannot be dropped, and the reported finding is module-level attribution rather than presence of the vulnerable code.
statements.action_statement: The assertion is based on the recorded link-graph evidence for both collector distributions and architectures. Re-evaluate and withdraw this statement if collector component selection or its x/crypto dependency graph changes. Retire it when scanner matching for this advisory becomes package-aware, or if upstream ever publishes a fixed x/crypto release.
